messages.author: 3f98c2cb066b2e7d
messages.subject: inset problem, new ggplot2 aesthetic?
parts:
Hello,

ggtree is a really awesome package!
I used to run the ggtree inset function without problem and now even the most basic attempt to use it now no longer works. (Last attempt which worked was Sept 27 and I experienced my first error message on Oct 18th).

I noticed there has been an update of ggplot2 over the summer with some consequence on aesthetics but I am not quite sure it is related.
Here is a basic example with what the console returns.
> set.seed(1)
> tr <- rtree(4)
> p <- ggtree(tr)
> pie <- nodepie(p$data, cols = 4:5)
this theme will be removed in next release
this theme was moved to ggimage::theme_transparent and will be removed in next release
this theme will be removed in next release
this theme was moved to ggimage::theme_transparent and will be removed in next release
this theme will be removed in next release
this theme was moved to ggimage::theme_transparent and will be removed in next release
this theme will be removed in next release
this theme was moved to ggimage::theme_transparent and will be removed in next release
this theme will be removed in next release
this theme was moved to ggimage::theme_transparent and will be removed in next release
this theme will be removed in next release
this theme was moved to ggimage::theme_transparent and will be removed in next release
this theme will be removed in next release
this theme was moved to ggimage::theme_transparent and will be removed in next release
> inset(p, pie)
The inset function will be defunct in next release, please use ggimage::geom_subview() instead.
The subview function will be defunct in next release, please use ggimage::geom_subview() instead.
The subview function will be defunct in next release, please use ggimage::geom_subview() instead.
Error: Aesthetics must be either length 1 or the same as the data (1): xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax


In the past, I would had the same error messages except for the very last one: Error: Aesthetics must be either length 1 or the same as the data (1): xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax
Any suggestion or quick fix for such an issue?
Thank you,

 
Ludo
